answer:
The radar's fastest-growing topics in the month before the 2 Dec 2001 bankruptcy were the Dynegy merger, contracts and master netting, and post-collapse messages. I took the window as 2 Nov to 2 Dec. Ken Lay's all-employee email of 2 Dec says Enron filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions that morning. The figures below come from the radar's `top_topics` and `topic_history` tools. They measure each topic's recent mail (the preceding four weeks) against the week ending 28 Oct.

Top of the list, by gain in recent mail:
- **Dynegy merger (topic 1505):** recent mail went from 0 to 1,149 (+1,149). The radar raised an alert for it in the week ending 18 Nov, at 145 times its normal level. Most of it is forwarded press: 939 of the 1,149 in the week ending 2 Dec. The top writers are the people circulating press digests (m..schmidt and courtney.votaw).
- **Contracts and master netting (topic 1418):** recent mail went from 123 to 911 (+788), with no press at all, so it is internal legal and contract traffic. The most active writers include Marie Heard, Sara Shackleton and Debra Perlingiere.
- **Messages after the collapse (topic 1485):** 0 to 249 (+249). It is mostly employee and Ken Lay messages.
- **Smaller risers:** EnronOnline and credit fears (+159), Fastow partnerships fallout (+154), Collateral and unpaid invoices (+152), Shareholder and 401(k) suits (+145), and Trade counts (+144).

What the mail in each of the top topics shows:
- **Dynegy:** The 28 Nov message from Lay said Dynegy is terminating the merger agreement and Enron's debt was downgraded to below investment grade by S&P, Moody's and Fitch. Employees wrote angrily about the merger, for example "I and everyone else out here want to be compensated for what has happened." One staffer wrote on 26 Nov: "40% chance we merge with Dynegy is what some people are saying. Bankruptcy is our other option."
- **Master netting:** Legal staff were rushing counterparty netting and close-out terms. Examples are a Duke Master Netting Agreement and a BNP Paribas Master Netting Agreement targeted for close of business on 27 Nov. A Dominion trader wrote on 29 Nov that the language on both the ISDA and the Master Netting Agreement had been agreed "but Enron is unwilling to sign either under the current circumstances."

Caveats:
- The radar's "growth" is measured from a late-October baseline, and several of these topics did not exist before November. Their jumps from 0 partly reflect the topic first appearing, not only a surge in volume.
- The Dynegy topic is largely press forwarded inside Enron. The contracts topic is the biggest rise that is entirely written by Enron's own people.
- `topic_history` shows no weekly row for the week ending 25 Nov in the contracts topic, so I can't give its full weekly path.

Subject: Enron Files Chapter 11 Reorganization
From: chairman.ken@enron.com
Date: 2001-12-02

-- We filed voluntary petitions for relief under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code. Contrary to popular belief, this does not mean we are out of business. What it does mean is that we have entered into a court-supervised process by which we can continue to operate most of our businesses, reorganize our finances, and explore various strategic, operational and financial alternatives, including the sale of non-core assets, in an orderly manner.

As you have heard, Dynegy is terminating the merger agreement today.  Among other things, this means we are now free to pursue other alternatives - which we are actively doing.  As a consequence of uncertainty about the deal - and now Dynegy's announcement - Enron's debt was downgraded to below investment grade levels today by S&P, Moody's and Fitch.

I and everyone else out here want to be compensated for what has happened - you had guys bailing out with $30+MM. They will be sitting high on the hog and we have people looking at a measley $15,000 plus the thought of losing their jobs with the merger.
40% chance we merge with Dynegy is what some people are saying.  Bankruptcy is our other option.

We are moving ahead with finalizing a Master Netting Agreement that will cover all physical and financial agreements between BNP Paribas and Enron, except for the exchange agreements pertaining to NYMEX and LME trading.  The agreements to be included under this arrangement are listed below.  The intent is to complete the agreement by close of business on Tuesday, November 27.  We have communicated this to Bart Schouest at BNP Paribas and to BNP Paribas' counsel in New York.

My phone message this morning relates to the Master Netting Agreement that

my understanding that the language on both the ISDA and the Master Netting
